title: Learning Team Session: the meter seal job and return to service, Hazira 2020
audience: A learning-team facilitator who did not investigate, and the people who do the meter seal work: mechanical maintenance fitters, an instrument technician, a gas-terminal field operator and a stores clerk
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before the session.

Scope chosen for this worked example: one activity, the gasket replacement on condensate meter 310FT01 and its return to service. The gap rows are the HFACS codes of the ten prompts kept, as printed by wai-wad; the ten prompts are the seal-job prompts among the 30 top-rated, with the topic after the colon shortened to the condition.
Who is in the room is the user's answer, by role only. The team's answers belong in learning-team-notes.csv, which the team fills in; this pack holds none.

bottom_line.text: For the meter seal job, the documents and the people's accounts describe different work: the session asks the fitters and operators how the job is really done, from the part to the test.
Start with the repeat reseals: three recorded gasket jobs in 22 months, each closed as routine.
Then return to service: what an operating-pressure test meant on the shift, when no procedure asked for a test to design pressure.

rows: Welcome, the ground rules and the banner read aloud
Set a learning frame: the team are the experts, no one is judged
Walk through a meter seal job as it normally goes, from the work order to return to service
Hear work as done before anyone opens a procedure
Learn how the seal is chosen and obtained in practice
Questions on testing and return to service
Learn what the test before return to service looks like on the shift
Soak: a short break, then what surprised the team
Let the first answers settle before anyone talks about fixes
What would make the seal job easier to do safely
Collect the team's own ideas for a second meeting; no decisions about people

items.text: The fitters, technicians and operators are the experts on this job: ask, listen and write down their words, not a summary of them.
Learn first and fix later: keep this meeting for discovery, and hold the fixes for a second meeting after a soak of a day or more.
Ask how the seal job normally goes on an ordinary shift, not only what happened in September 2020.
Read each question as written and let the team answer it; the export's wording behind it is in the why line, not a view to defend.
The team records its answers, in its own words, in learning-team-notes.csv; the facilitator does not fill in the answer column for them.
